stem: Which of the following amines has the smallest $pK_b$ in water?

verdicts.working: 2-Phenylethan-1-amine is an aliphatic amine, whose nitrogen lone pair is more available for protonation than in the aniline derivatives. It is therefore the strongest base and has the smallest pKb.

working:
In 2-phenylethan-1-amine, the nitrogen lone pair is not conjugated with the phenyl ring.
In the aromatic amines, the lone pair is delocalised into the ring; the nitro group further reduces its availability.
Greater availability of the lone pair gives a stronger base and a smaller $pK_b$.
Thus, 2-phenylethan-1-amine has the smallest $pK_b$.

Independent check: 2-Phenylethan-1-amine is an aliphatic amine, whose nitrogen lone pair is more available for protonation than in the aniline derivatives. It is therefore the strongest base and has the smallest pKb.
solution:
The nitrogen lone pair in 2-phenylethan-1-amine is not conjugated with the phenyl ring, so it is more available for protonation than in the aromatic amines.
Greater basicity corresponds to smaller $pK_b$; hence 2-phenylethan-1-amine has the smallest $pK_b$. (B)
